title: Code to Nowhere
subtitle: Leak an authorization code through Kestrel's open redirect
summary: Kestrel's OAuth broker accepts any redirect_uri. Send a code to an attacker-controlled host, capture the marker, then enforce the registered callback.
scenario: Kestrel Identity brokers logins for its own web client. The authorize endpoint never compares redirect_uri with the registered value. Demonstrate the leak and close it without breaking the real client.
learningObjectives: Explain why redirect_uri must be matched exactly
Capture a code delivered to an unregistered host
authorizedScope: Only the Kestrel training broker. No real identity provider is involved.
riskSummary: An unvalidated redirect_uri lets attackers receive authorization codes, which they exchange for tokens and account access.
remediation: Compare the full redirect URI byte-for-byte against client registration, reject look-alike prefixes, and bind codes to client_id plus PKCE.
conclusion: You redirected an authorization code to an unregistered host and then restricted the broker to the registered callback.

objectives.title: Steal a code
objectives.description: Call /oauth/authorize with an attacker-controlled redirect_uri and submit the marker embedded in the issued code.

hints.text: Use `curl -si` and read the Location header: `?redirect_uri=https://attacker.example/collect`.

objectives.title: Enforce the registered callback
objectives.description: Turn on redirect validation. The live check confirms unregistered hosts (including prefix look-alikes) are rejected while the registered callback still receives a code.

criteria: registered callback still gets a code

walkthrough.title: Inspect the client
walkthrough.body: The landing page shows the registered callback.

walkthrough.title: Redirect the code
walkthrough.body: Send the code to an unregistered host.
